title: State of art of AI RPG/Adventure
author: gcampos
selftext:
I was wondering what are the best games in the market right now that use AI for NPC conversations or sort of like a "game master".

I did a look myself and most of the things I can find are role play games about talking with a particular character, but nothing that feels like a tabletop RPG or uses the NPC conversations in a unique way.

comments.author: ffxivthrowaway03
comments.body: Biggest production example is probably Where Winds Meet.  There's a sidequest feature that uses LLM chatbots for you to talk to in-game NPCs as a minigame to convince each one of something.  It works ok-ish, but the guardrails are very tight and the rough localization causes it to frequently get locked in logic loops or repeat itself.

replies.author: gcampos
replies.body: Interesting, do you know if they used a local LLM or an online one?

comments.author: bingewavecinema
comments.body: This one, you can talk with them in real time: [https://www.glitch.fun/games/42de534c-600f-4228-af9e-b69faef94cce/play](https://www.glitch.fun/games/42de534c-600f-4228-af9e-b69faef94cce/play)

replies.author: gcampos
replies.body: I will give it a try

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body: I don’t think anyone has really figured out this one yet. There’s a bigger discussion here—how do you have an open-ended discussion with an NPC while still keeping the game’s story on track? If the NPC makes stuff up that’s not in the game, you’re gonna end up with confused and disappointed players. Then there’s the actual mechanics of running this—right now it is risky to stick a remote LLM in your game and let users prompt it, and local LLMs are either inconveniently large or not very powerful.

replies.author: gcampos
replies.body: That is good to know, I thought I was missing something

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body: I have a LLM powered text game and this is exactly the primary issue. Giving players agency while moving a story along is a very delicate balance.  Some players want a sandbox to play in, others want a story thst moves at a good pace. Very hard to make both groups happy.

replies.author: gcampos
replies.body: What is your game? Did you release it?

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body: It's just an online text game, not really trying to be a full on RPG, more of a text adventure with RPG elements.  https://nervejack.gg

comments.author: RuinousFate
comments.body: Tokens will have to be cheaper and models will need to be far better tuned before we reach a good level for this.

replies.author: gcampos
replies.body: I'm not so sure, I tried some local LLM for chatting and they can hold a conversation quite well, I dont think we are too far from it

replies.author: RuinousFate
replies.body: For NPCs, you'd want consistency for their character, role in the world and supposed experiences in said world (history).

comments.author: Character_Cup58
comments.body: Talesrpg is quite good, by playing you advance story. Has lots of features including dnd mode, attributes, health... it is possible to give instructions to AI in later chapters like plot twists. Also some stories have customized states ai tracks during play (still limited to 6 now) like reputation, companions, spells, etc (of course it is all just textual).

replies.author: gcampos
replies.body: I will check this one out

comments.author: silly_bet_3454
comments.body:
Just want to point out the distinction between using AI to develop a regular game, or in this case to generate tons of content for NPC convos, versus wiring an LLM directly into the game itself. They are extremely different things in practice.

Using an LLM within the game at runtime is an interesting idea, but I wouldn't personally want to mess with that, it's gonna be messy. But if you were gonna do it, I think it would be interesting to see if you can just run a local model (assuming you have some decent hardware on which the game itself is running) and how far you could go with that, managing resources between the LLM and the game would be tough, but then you have full control and don't have to deal with some API that costs money or whatever

replies.author: gcampos
replies.body: I think you thought the things I was thinking too. Even if technically would be possible to make a good experience with a frontier model, its unlikely the experience would justify the cost

comments.author: ilganeli
comments.body:
We have been working on building this shape of experience for a little while now (alongside developing game engine, assets pipelines, etc.) . Our focus has been on minimizing AI slop and presenting a curated storytelling experience. You're welcome to try out what we have at [https://fabletable.ai](https://fabletable.ai) . It's free to play as we build out the game. 

If interested in some of the tooling, a lot of the engineering harness we've used to scale our development is open sourced at [https://github.com/organizations/Boundless-Studios](https://github.com/organizations/Boundless-Studios)
